h1: SME Policy: Quality, Health, Safety and Environment at Steel Mind Engineers
quickAnswer: The SME Policy of Steel Mind Engineers sets the rules for quality control, health and safety, and environmental care in the workshop and on site.
alt: Supervisor inspecting a steel connection on a safe construction site.

blocks.title: Why Steel Mind Engineers Has This Policy

blocks.text: In steel construction, one poorly welded joint or one unsupervised lift can injure people and cost a client years of investment. The way a company manages quality, health, safety and the environment therefore affects the quality of its structures. The SME Policy sets the rules for the workshop, the site crews and the company's dealings with clients and suppliers.

Steel Mind Engineers inspects material when it arrives, checks dimensions after cutting, examines welds before assembly and checks alignment during erection. When a result falls short of the specification, the correction is recorded.

Every employee is trained before working on site. Workers wear certified protective equipment and follow written site rules. Risk reviews take place regularly so that hazards are removed instead of tolerated.

Cutting layouts are planned to reduce scrap, and offcuts are sent for recycling. Welding fumes and paint overspray are controlled. Working methods are chosen to limit noise, dust and waste at the workshop and on client premises.
Steel Mind Engineers follows the quality, environmental and workplace safety rules that apply to its operations. It keeps the records needed to show that compliance to clients and authorities.

Feedback from clients, supervisors and workers is collected after each project and turned into changes in procedure. Management is responsible for applying the policy. Every employee has the right and the duty to stop work that looks unsafe and to report it.
